items.sentence: Everyone in our section ___ a group chat for homework.
items.why: Everyone is singular, so use 'has'.

items.sentence: Jom and Lyka ___ basketball at the covered court every afternoon.
items.why: Two subjects joined by 'and' are plural, so use 'play'.

items.sentence: Nobody in the jeepney ___ coins for the fare.
items.why: Nobody is singular, so use 'has'.

items.sentence: There ___ three tricycles waiting outside the school gate.
items.why: 'Three tricycles' is plural, so use 'there are'.

items.sentence: Each student ___ a copy of the module before the quiz.
items.why: Each is singular, so the verb takes 's': 'needs'.

items.sentence: Either Marco or his cousins ___ bringing the speaker to the fiesta.
items.why: With 'or', the verb matches the closer subject 'cousins', so use 'are'.

items.sentence: There ___ a sari-sari store beside Tita Nena's house.
items.why: 'A sari-sari store' is one thing, so use 'there is'.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron and his friends ___ online games until midnight.
items.why: 'Kuya Ron and his friends' is plural, so use 'play' with no 's'.

items.sentence: Everybody in the barangay ___ ready for the typhoon.
items.why: Everybody is singular, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Each of the players ___ a new jersey for the game.
items.why: 'Each' is the subject and it is singular, so use 'wants'.

items.sentence: The dog wagged ___ tail when Bea came home from school.
items.why: 'Its' without an apostrophe shows that the tail belongs to the dog.

items.sentence: ___ going to the mall after class, right?
items.why: 'You're' means 'you are', which fits before 'going'.

items.sentence: The students left ___ bags under the mango tree.
items.why: 'Their' shows the bags belong to the students.

items.sentence: ___ phone is this on the teacher's table?
items.why: 'Whose' asks who owns something.

items.sentence: ___ almost time for merienda, so let's finish the quiz.
items.why: 'It's' means 'it is', which fits before 'almost time'.

items.sentence: ___ the one who won the free load from the store raffle.
items.why: 'Who's' means 'who is', which fits before 'the one'.

items.sentence: ___ jeepney fare went up again this week.
items.why: 'Your' shows the fare belongs to you; 'you're' means 'you are'.

items.sentence: ___ mother works as a nurse in Dubai.
items.why: Add 's to a name to show that something belongs to that person.

items.sentence: Look, ___ waiting for us at the tricycle stop!
items.why: 'They're' means 'they are', which fits before 'waiting'.

items.sentence: Many ___ in this class have OFW parents.
items.why: A plural noun just adds 's' with no apostrophe when nothing is owned.

items.sentence: Yesterday, Jom ___ his load at the sari-sari store.
items.why: 'Yesterday' tells you it already happened, so use the past form 'bought'.

items.sentence: Right now, the students ___ for the fiesta parade.
items.why: 'Right now' means it is happening at this moment, so use 'are practicing'.

items.sentence: Every day, Tita Nena ___ the store at six in the morning.
items.why: 'Every day' shows a habit, so use the simple present 'opens'.

items.sentence: Last night, a strong typhoon ___ our barangay.
items.why: 'Last night' is finished time, so use the past form 'hit'.

items.sentence: Marco ___ a TikTok video right now, so be quiet.
items.why: 'Right now' means the action is going on, so use 'is filming'.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron ___ to work by jeepney every morning.
items.why: 'Every morning' shows a habit, so use the simple present 'goes'.

items.sentence: Bea ___ the basketball game yesterday because of the rain.
items.why: 'Yesterday' is past time, so use 'missed'.

items.sentence: The tricycle drivers ___ under the tree right now.
items.why: 'Right now' means it is happening now, so use 'are resting'.

items.sentence: Lyka ___ her mother in Dubai every Sunday on video call.
items.why: 'Every Sunday' shows a habit, and Lyka is singular, so use 'calls'.

items.sentence: Two days ago, our class ___ the reading test.
items.why: 'Two days ago' is past time, so use 'took'.

items.sentence: Our classes start ___ seven in the morning.
items.why: Use 'at' for an exact time like seven o'clock.

items.sentence: The town fiesta is ___ May every year.
items.why: Use 'in' for months, years and seasons.

items.sentence: The basketball game is ___ Saturday afternoon.
items.why: Use 'on' for days of the week and dates.

items.sentence: Tita Nena lives ___ Davao City now.
items.why: Use 'in' for cities, provinces and countries.

items.sentence: Bea bought a cake ___ her best friend's birthday.
items.why: Use 'for' to show the purpose or the person something is meant for.

items.sentence: Jom gave his seat ___ an old woman in the jeepney.
items.why: Use 'to' after 'give' to show who receives something.

items.sentence: The students are waiting ___ the school gate.
items.why: Use 'at' for a specific point or spot like a gate.

items.sentence: Share the merienda ___ the two of you.
items.why: Use 'between' for two people or things.

items.sentence: The coach divided the jerseys ___ all the players.
items.why: Use 'among' for three or more people or things.

items.sentence: The teacher wrote the quiz answers ___ the board.
items.why: Use 'on' for a surface like a board, wall or table.
